origins.section: The Knapsack Cannot See Time or Crews
The Crews Change the Plan: Two Circuits Out, Two In
Three Tests State the Crew Rule

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-season-row: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-season-row: But the supervisor books months, not seasons. A month has 8 crew-weeks, and three of the first plan's circuits need 7 each (C04, C12, C17), which leaves 1 crew-week in each of their months for the six other circuits
recorded.prompt:q-month-objective: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-month-objective: Moving C12 from month 1 to month 6 removes the same risk, so the solver picks months only to make the packing work, and any month that packs is as good as any other.
recorded.prompt:q-paired-tests: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-paired-tests: The pair is deliberate: the same two circuits, one month refused and two months allowed. A model with no crew rows passes neither the first nor (since it has no months) the second.
